idiom_name: typing.Optional with generator expressions and dataclasses.replace
implementation_notes: Python has no optic type: the 0..1 focus is typing.Optional[T] (or T | None) plus an explicit is-not-None test, and the plural traversal is a generator expression or comprehension that filters and maps in one pass, with itertools.chain/chain.from_iterable for flattening nested iterables lazily. For immutable-style updates dataclasses.replace returns a new instance with selected fields replaced, which is the closest standard-library equivalent of set-over-a-focus; these idioms replace the classic structure. A helper or library is justified only when the same derived path is read and updated from many places.
code_sketch:
city: str = order.customer.city if order.customer else "unknown"

# 0..n: update present lines, keep order
repriced = [dataclasses.replace(l, price=discount(l.price))
            for l in order.lines if l is not None]
total = sum(l.price for l in order.lines if l is not None)
pitfalls: Optional annotations are not enforced: order.customer.city raises AttributeError at runtime when the intermediate is None, and type checkers flag it only under strict optional settings.
Generators are lazy and single-use: a traversal built as a generator that is consumed twice silently yields nothing the second time.
dataclasses.replace performs a shallow copy: nested mutable fields are shared with the original, so the pure update can still mutate the old value.
